subject: Audit streaming & trace-hook handoff for private deployment
messages:
From: Tim Olson <tim.olson@acme-corp.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Security <security@acme-corp.com>
Date: 2028-07-18T09:32:00-07:00
Subject: Observability evidence for our private VPC deployment

Jonas,

Thanks for the call earlier. As part of Acme's security review we need a concise evidence bundle showing how Redwood will ship logs/traces from our private VPC into our SIEM. Key constraints below — please confirm what you can deliver and the format: 

- Transport: Syslog over TLS (RFC 5425) preferred; Splunk HEC over mutual TLS acceptable. No direct internet egress except to approved endpoints.
- Evidence: sample configs, firewall rules (ports/IP ranges), proof of token handling + rotation, retained sample logs (redacted), and a proof-of-delivery timeline.
- Tracing: header mappings for distributed traces, span sanitizer rules, and guidance on sampling to avoid PII leakage.
- Timeline: procurement needs this by EOD next Friday (2028-07-25).

Can you confirm delivery format (tar.gz preferred) and whether you need our Ops contact to open firewall ports?

Tim Olson
Sr. Security Engineer
Acme Corp
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Tim Olson <tim.olson@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-18T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Observability evidence for our private VPC deployment

Tim — thanks, we can meet that. High-level plan: 

1) Evidence bundle: tar.gz containing sample syslog TLS config, Splunk HEC example (mutual TLS), redacted log samples, firewall CIDR and ports, and a short README with delivery timestamps.
2) Transport options: we prefer in-VPC forwarder to your Splunk HEC (mutual TLS) or a TLS syslog stream to your collector. Both avoid general internet egress.
3) Token handling: we will include our token lifecycle doc and a code snippet showing HEC token rotation via Vault.
4) Trace hooks: sample trace header mapping and an extractor that strips PII fields; suggested sampling strategy (0.1% baseline, 5% for error traces).

Marissa and Ben — please prepare the artifacts below, and Soojin can validate the trace sanitizer rules against our privacy checklist.

Jonas
Head of Observability Partnerships
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Tim Olson <tim.olson@acme-corp.com>
Date: 2028-07-22T13:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Observability evidence for our private VPC deployment

Tim (cc team) — attached is a short HEC example and token rotation snippet. Key notes: 

- We recommend HEC over mTLS for delivery if you need structured events; our forwarder supports both.
- Token rotation approach: issue short-lived HEC tokens with Vault TTL 24h, automated rotation job runs every 12h; tokens stored in your KMS.
- We also include a delivery proof script that tail -f's a sample log and reports HEC ack timestamps to a local file for auditor review.

Sample firewall guidance (ops note): allow outbound from forwarder IPs to your HEC IPs on port 8088/tcp and allow return traffic; for syslog TLS use 6514/tcp. No egress to other destinations required.

Onboarding next steps: if you want, I can loop Splunk onboarding for a short handshake to validate HEC certs.

Ben Carter
Senior Integration Engineer
Redwood Inference
